title_ar: حكم اجتماع الرجال والنساء تحت سقف واحد لعمل معين
title_en: The Ruling on Men and Women Gathering under One Roof for a Particular Task
body_ar: السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته شيخنا أحد الإخوة يسأل عن حكم اجتماع الرجال والنساء تحت سقف واحد لعمل معين.. وعن حكم عادة دخول الأجانب منازل فيها أجنبيات الجواب و عليكم السلام و رحمة الله و بركاته لم تكن البيوت في العهد النبوي إلا حُجَرا أي غرفا يجتمع الرجال و النساء في كل غرفة و قد شرع الله الاستئذان في ثلاث ساعات لذلك و كذلك كان النساء يصلين مع الرجال في مسجد رسول الله صلى الله عليه و سلم فكان يأمر الرجال أن لا ينصرفوا حتى ينصرف النساء و يأمر النساء أن لا يرفعن من السجود حتى يجلس الرجال لئلا ينكشف شيء من عورات الرجال لكن لهذا الاجتماع ضوابط منها عدم خلوة أجنبي بأجنبية مطلقا و ستر النساء ما أوجب الله عليهن ستره و عدم تطيبهن و عدم الخضوع بالقول و الكلام في الريبة و الله أعلم
body_en:
Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings. Our Sheikh, one of the brothers asks about the ruling on men and women gathering under one roof for a particular task… and about the ruling on the customary practice of unrelated men entering houses in which there are unrelated women.

Answer: And upon you be peace, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

In the prophetic era the houses were nothing but ḥujar — that is, single rooms — in which men and women gathered in every room; and it was for that reason that God laid down the seeking of permission at three hours. Likewise the women used to pray together with the men in the mosque of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and he would order the men not to leave until the women had left, and would order the women not to raise their heads from the prostration until the men had sat up, so that nothing of the men's nakedness should be exposed.

But this gathering has governing conditions. Among them: that there be no private seclusion (khalwah) between an unrelated man and an unrelated woman at all; that the women cover what God has obliged them to cover; that they not wear perfume; and that there be no softness of speech, and no speech in which there is anything suspect. And God knows best.

flags.context: لم تكن البيوت في العهد النبوي إلا حُجَرا أي غرفا
options: the apartments of the Prophet's household
flags.note: The Sheikh glosses the word himself, so the English keeps both his term and his gloss. The argument depends on the gloss: a house was a single room, so men and women of the household were necessarily together in it, which is why a rule of seeking permission was needed rather than a rule of separation.

flags.arabic: شرع الله الاستئذان في ثلاث ساعات
flags.context: و قد شرع الله الاستئذان في ثلاث ساعات لذلك
options: the three times of privacy laid down in Sūrat al-Nūr 24:58
three hours of the day, unspecified
flags.note: The reference is to the three times at which permission must be sought before entering — before the dawn prayer, at midday, and after the night prayer. The Sheikh does not cite the verse and the English does not supply it in the text; recorded here so a reviewer can add the citation if the office wants one.

translator_notes: The structure of the answer matters and has been kept: first the historical point that mixing under one roof was the normal condition in the Prophet's time and was regulated rather than barred, then the conditions that govern it. Taking either half alone misrepresents him.
The questioner asked two questions — gathering for a task, and men entering houses where there are unrelated women. The answer treats them together and does not separate them.
عورات الرجال rendered 'the men's nakedness', the parts required to be covered; the detail is the Sheikh's own explanation for the order about rising from prostration.
الخضوع بالقول ('softness of speech') is the phrase of Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:32, used here without citation; compare record 936 in this slice, where he quotes the verse itself.
